claim_policy: Evidence is platform- and query-specific. Never describe a rank as globally most-used.

sources.scope: Official behavior for trending, search, locale, ratings, and canonical URLs
Candidate names and commonly understood translations used by the museum project
Contextual reply selection and safety evidence from 1.56M conversation turns
Annual GIPHY editorial and platform metrics signal

entries.label: Hamster running on a wheel
entries.alt: A hamster runs rapidly inside an exercise wheel.
entries.use: Start a work sprint or joke about repetitive effort.
entries.avoid: Avoid when workload or burnout is a serious concern.

entries.label: Mouse sprinting in a wheel
entries.alt: A small mouse runs fast in a wheel without moving forward.
entries.use: Show frantic motion, repeated work, or effort without progress.
entries.avoid: Avoid as praise for meaningful progress.

entries.label: Cat working at a computer
entries.alt: A cat works busily at a computer.
entries.use: Signal that work is underway with upbeat energy.
entries.avoid: Avoid in formal status reporting where a concrete update is needed.

entries.label: Shiba Inu typing from the couch
entries.alt: A Shiba Inu under a blanket taps lazily on a laptop.
entries.use: Start remote work or admit to working with low energy.
entries.avoid: Avoid when you need to project urgency or authority.
entries.search: shiba dog typing work from home

entries.label: Processing and buffering spinner
entries.alt: A circular loading indicator spins continuously.
entries.use: Signal processing, thinking, or a harmless delay without sarcasm.
entries.avoid: Avoid when someone needs an actual ETA or incident update.

entries.label: Skeleton still waiting
entries.alt: A skeleton rests its head on one hand while waiting at a table.
entries.use: Exaggerate a long, low-stakes wait among peers.
entries.avoid: Avoid with clients, reports, or anyone responsible for a stressful delay.

entries.label: Pablo Escobar waiting alone
entries.alt: A man sits alone on a swing and looks down while waiting.
entries.use: Portray an extended wait or being left alone in a low-stakes situation.
entries.avoid: Avoid for real isolation, grief, or serious mental-health contexts.

entries.label: Spanky bored at a desk
entries.alt: A child props up his head and taps impatiently on a desk.
entries.use: Show mild boredom or waiting without high drama.
entries.avoid: Avoid when impatience could pressure or embarrass the recipient.

entries.label: Clock showing time running out
entries.alt: An illustrated clock emphasizes that time is running out.
entries.use: Lightly mark an approaching deadline without blaming anyone.
entries.avoid: Avoid instead of a clear deadline, owner, or risk statement.

entries.label: Overloaded multitasking
entries.alt: A person rapidly handles several tasks at once.
entries.use: Admit to juggling many low-stakes tasks.
entries.avoid: Avoid when overload requires escalation or workload changes.

entries.label: SpongeBob working overtime
entries.alt: SpongeBob reacts to working overtime.
entries.use: Joke with peers about a late work session.
entries.avoid: Avoid normalizing compulsory overtime or serious burnout.

entries.label: Monday coffee motivation
entries.alt: A morning coffee animation offers weekday motivation.
entries.use: Open a weekday work session with gentle energy.
entries.avoid: Avoid assuming everyone drinks coffee.

entries.label: Leaving work on Friday
entries.alt: A rally car speeds away through sand with text about leaving work Friday.
entries.use: Celebrate wrapping up work for the week.
entries.avoid: Avoid when teammates still face an urgent incident or deadline.

entries.label: Friends working together
entries.alt: A group collaborates together as a team.
entries.use: Reinforce collaboration or a shared start.
entries.avoid: Avoid as a substitute for naming actual collaborators or credit.

entries.label: Deploy it now
entries.alt: An animated prompt says to deploy the release now.
entries.use: Celebrate a release decision after checks have passed.
entries.avoid: Never use as authorization to bypass review, tests, or change controls.

entries.label: Vintage debugging session
entries.alt: A vintage scene represents fixing a bug in production.
entries.use: Signal that debugging is underway after the situation is stable.
entries.avoid: Avoid during an active high-severity incident or customer harm.

entries.label: Frustrated at the computer
entries.alt: A person reacts angrily to a computer.
entries.use: Vent lightly about a machine or bug, not a person.
entries.avoid: Avoid when anger could be read as directed at a teammate.

entries.label: Literal FedEx ship-it joke
entries.alt: A FedEx shipping scene turns the phrase ship it into a visual pun.
entries.use: Mark a completed software release with a literal pun.
entries.avoid: Avoid before release approval or when shipping means physical logistics.

entries.label: GIPHY QA: it works
entries.alt: A GIPHY QA reaction celebrates that something works.
entries.use: Celebrate a fix or passing test after verifying it.
entries.avoid: Avoid declaring success before validation is complete.

entries.label: This Is Fine dog in a fire
entries.alt: A cartoon dog calmly drinks while the room burns and says, This is fine.
entries.use: Acknowledge obvious low-stakes chaos or ironic denial among peers.
entries.avoid: Avoid during emergencies, safety incidents, customer harm, or real crisis.

entries.label: Brace yourself, here we go
entries.alt: A reaction braces for another familiar round of events.
entries.use: Start a familiar recurring task or react to a repeated pattern.
entries.avoid: Avoid when it could belittle a person's repeated concern.
entries.search: here we go again brace yourself

entries.label: Frustrated deep breath
entries.alt: A person pauses and takes a deep breath while frustrated.
entries.use: Show yourself regrouping before continuing.
entries.avoid: Avoid telling an upset recipient to calm down.

entries.label: Kermit flailing excitedly
entries.alt: Kermit waves his arms wildly in excitement or panic.
entries.use: Express comic overexcitement or harmless panic.
entries.avoid: Avoid when urgency is real or instructions must remain clear.

entries.label: Homer disappearing into a hedge
entries.alt: Homer Simpson slowly backs into a hedge and disappears.
entries.use: Withdraw from an awkward moment or retract a harmless comment.
entries.avoid: Avoid evading responsibility, feedback, or a request for help.

entries.label: Awkward kid smile
entries.alt: A child gives an uncertain, awkward smile.
entries.use: Acknowledge a harmless awkward pause or uncertain reaction.
entries.avoid: Do not use to mock a child, appearance, or vulnerable person.

entries.label: Cute character says you can do it
entries.alt: A cute crocheted character offers an encouraging you-can-do-it message.
entries.use: Encourage someone before a manageable challenge.
entries.avoid: Avoid minimizing a serious obstacle or replacing practical help.
entries.search: you can do it cute encouragement

entries.label: Proud of you reaction
entries.alt: A warm reaction communicates pride in the recipient.
entries.use: Celebrate someone else's effort or growth.
entries.avoid: Avoid a patronizing tone with senior colleagues or strangers.

entries.label: Top Gun high five
entries.alt: Two pilots walk together and exchange an excited high five.
entries.use: Celebrate a shared win or collaboration.
entries.avoid: Avoid taking credit from people who did the work.

entries.label: Well done gold star
entries.alt: A gold star marked Well done spins as colorful fireworks appear.
entries.use: Offer clear, accessible praise with low cultural ambiguity.
entries.avoid: Avoid if a gold-star motif could feel patronizing.

entries.label: The Office group party dance
entries.alt: Coworkers dance together under colorful office party lights.
entries.use: Celebrate a team win with a familiar workplace reference.
entries.avoid: Avoid when only part of the team benefited or someone is excluded.

entries.label: Erin's huge fist-pump celebration
entries.alt: Erin from The Office jumps up and pumps both fists with excitement.
entries.use: Celebrate a big, unambiguously positive result.
entries.avoid: Avoid for modest achievements or solemn announcements.
entries.search: The Office Erin excited fist pump

entries.label: RuPaul applause
entries.alt: RuPaul applauds enthusiastically.
entries.use: Give lively approval or congratulations.
entries.avoid: Avoid if the reference is unfamiliar and a neutral applause GIF would be clearer.

entries.label: Denzel Washington: OK, alright
entries.alt: Denzel Washington nods and says, OK, alright.
entries.use: Acknowledge a good point or accept a plan with relaxed confidence.
entries.avoid: Avoid if the nod could read as dismissive or overly performative.

entries.label: Robert Redford's approving nod
entries.alt: A bearded Robert Redford smiles and nods with quiet approval.
entries.use: Offer understated approval or recognition.
entries.avoid: Do not misidentify the actor as Zach Galifianakis in the explanation.

entries.label: Brent Rambo computer-kid thumbs up
entries.alt: A child at a computer smiles and gives a thumbs up.
entries.use: Give retro, friendly approval, especially in technical chats.
entries.avoid: Avoid when a plain acknowledgement would be more professional.
entries.search: Brent Rambo thumbs up computer kid

entries.label: Dwight's emotional thank you
entries.alt: Dwight from The Office looks moved and says, Thank you.
entries.use: Offer grateful thanks with light dramatic emphasis.
entries.avoid: Avoid when the thanks should be formal or very specific.

entries.label: Kazoo Kid: thanks, partner
entries.alt: A child in a forest warmly says, I just wanted to say thanks, partner.
entries.use: Thank a peer or friend with deliberately wholesome humor.
entries.avoid: Avoid if the childlike tone could seem patronizing.

entries.label: Nick Offerman's shy thank you
entries.alt: Nick Offerman smiles shyly, lifts his shoulders, and says, Thank you.
entries.use: Accept praise or say thanks without sounding grandiose.
entries.avoid: Avoid when concise formal thanks is expected.

entries.label: Dr. Evil welcomes you
entries.alt: Dr. Evil opens his arms with the word Welcome.
entries.use: Welcome someone into an informal group or recurring joke.
entries.avoid: Avoid when the villain reference could make onboarding feel hostile.

entries.label: Simple animated sorry
entries.alt: A simple animation communicates Sorry.
entries.use: Accompany a minor, low-stakes apology after clearly naming the mistake.
entries.avoid: Never use as the whole response to real harm, conflict, or a high-stakes failure.

entries.label: Leonardo DiCaprio raises a glass
entries.alt: Leonardo DiCaprio smiles and raises a glass in a toast.
entries.use: Toast a success or congratulate someone informally.
entries.avoid: Avoid alcohol imagery with minors, recovery contexts, or unknown audiences.

entries.label: Orson Welles' intense applause
entries.alt: Orson Welles gives serious, emphatic applause in Citizen Kane.
entries.use: Applaud an impressive point with old-cinema gravitas.
entries.avoid: Clarify intent if it might read as sarcastic slow applause.

entries.label: Kids join a joyful classroom dance
entries.alt: One child dances on a chair and another joins in enthusiastically.
entries.use: Celebrate contagious enthusiasm or someone joining the effort.
entries.avoid: Do not use to ridicule the children or their movement.

entries.label: Elmo's gleeful dance
entries.alt: Elmo throws his arms up and dances with delight.
entries.use: Express uncomplicated joy with a broadly legible character.
entries.avoid: Avoid when a childlike tone would undermine the message.

entries.label: Robert De Niro: you're good
entries.alt: Robert De Niro gives a reassuring you're-good reaction.
entries.use: Reassure a peer that things are acceptable or settled.
entries.avoid: Inspect the clip first; avoid with unknown audiences or a G-only requirement.

entries.label: Borat: great success
entries.alt: Borat celebrates and declares a great success.
entries.use: Celebrate an obvious win among people who share the reference.
entries.avoid: Avoid with unknown audiences or where the character's caricature is unwelcome.

entries.label: Bryan Cranston mic drop
entries.alt: Bryan Cranston leans aside and casually drops a microphone.
entries.use: Cap a genuinely strong point or achievement.
entries.avoid: Avoid in disagreement where it would shut down discussion or gloat.

entries.label: Frank Reynolds recoils: nope
entries.alt: Danny DeVito recoils, shakes his head quickly, and says, Nope.
entries.use: Reject a harmless idea or react to something comically alarming.
entries.avoid: Avoid rejecting a person's vulnerable contribution or request.

entries.label: Bugs Bunny says no
entries.alt: Bugs Bunny looks smug while the letters N and O move below his mouth.
entries.use: Give an unambiguous low-stakes no with cartoon humor.
entries.avoid: Avoid when a respectful explanation or consent boundary deserves words.

entries.label: Michael Scott: no, please no
entries.alt: Michael Scott reacts with escalating horror and repeatedly says no.
entries.use: Exaggerate dread at a harmless recurrence among peers.
entries.avoid: Avoid direct feedback to a person or a serious negative decision.
entries.search: Michael Scott no god please no

entries.label: Captain Picard facepalm
entries.alt: Captain Picard lowers his head into his hand in exasperation.
entries.use: React to your own harmless mistake or an obviously flawed situation.
entries.avoid: Avoid humiliating the person who made a mistake.

entries.label: The Naked Gun group facepalm
entries.alt: One facepalm expands to a control room and then an entire audience facepalming.
entries.use: Exaggerate a collective reaction to a harmless, obvious blunder.
entries.avoid: Avoid piling on an individual mistake or public embarrassment.

entries.label: Puzzled little girl
entries.alt: A little girl stares ahead with a puzzled expression.
entries.use: Show straightforward confusion with little cultural knowledge required.
entries.avoid: Do not use to mock a child or imply another person is childish.

entries.label: Confused math lady
entries.alt: A woman looks around suspiciously as mathematical equations float in front of her.
entries.use: React to a complicated explanation or joke about overanalysis.
entries.avoid: Avoid implying a specific person cannot understand basic information.

entries.label: Steve Brule looks around confused
entries.alt: Steve Brule glances in every direction with a lost expression.
entries.use: Express being completely lost in a casual discussion.
entries.avoid: Avoid mocking another person's confusion.

entries.label: Blinking white guy
entries.alt: A man blinks twice with a surprised, incredulous look.
entries.use: React to an unexpected or contradictory statement.
entries.avoid: Avoid using the meme's racialized label in user-facing prose; describe the action instead.

entries.label: Fry narrows his eyes suspiciously
entries.alt: Fry from Futurama narrows his eyes in suspicion.
entries.use: Show light skepticism toward a claim or ambiguous situation.
entries.avoid: Avoid implying dishonesty in a high-stakes or interpersonal dispute.
entries.search: Futurama Fry suspicious not sure if

entries.label: Monkey puppet side-eye
entries.alt: A monkey puppet glances sideways nervously and then looks away.
entries.use: React to an awkward implication without targeting a person's identity.
entries.avoid: Avoid when silence could look evasive or complicit.

entries.label: Stanley rolls his eyes
entries.alt: Stanley from The Office rolls his eyes with deep exasperation.
entries.use: React to a recurring nuisance among peers who share the joke.
entries.avoid: Avoid directing contempt at a colleague; consider an animation or animal alternative to reduce stereotype risk.

entries.label: Nathan Fillion is speechless
entries.alt: Nathan Fillion starts to answer, stops, and remains speechless.
entries.use: Show that a low-stakes statement is too baffling to answer.
entries.avoid: Avoid dismissing sincere questions or feedback.

entries.label: Tim and Eric mind blown
entries.alt: A man's head appears to explode into a cosmic mind-blown effect.
entries.use: React to a surprising insight or clever reveal.
entries.avoid: Avoid a PG result or visually intense loop with sensitive audiences.

entries.label: Dramatic chipmunk turn
entries.alt: A prairie dog suddenly turns toward the camera with a dramatic zoom.
entries.use: Mark a sudden reveal or mock-dramatic turn.
entries.avoid: Avoid if the old reference will be less legible than a literal surprise GIF.

entries.label: Tyra Banks: we were rooting for you
entries.alt: Tyra Banks speaks angrily and emphatically about having rooted for someone.
entries.use: Exaggerate mock disappointment with close friends who know the reference.
entries.avoid: Avoid workplace feedback, real betrayal, or using a Black woman's anger as a generic caricature.
entries.search: Tyra Banks we were rooting for you

entries.label: David Tennant devastated in the rain
entries.alt: David Tennant stands in the rain looking quietly devastated.
entries.use: Exaggerate mild disappointment in a fictional or low-stakes context.
entries.avoid: Never use for grief, serious loss, illness, or trauma.
entries.search: David Tennant sad rain Doctor Who

entries.label: George Michael collapses in defeat
entries.alt: George Michael from Arrested Development lies down in comic defeat.
entries.use: React to your own low-stakes defeat or exhaustion.
entries.avoid: Avoid mocking another person's failure or real distress.

entries.label: Comic scream for help
entries.alt: A person screams for help in an exaggerated reaction.
entries.use: Exaggerate harmless overwhelm in a clearly playful exchange.
entries.avoid: Avoid emergencies, mental-health crises, or an actual request for help.

entries.label: Michael Jackson eating popcorn
entries.alt: Michael Jackson grins and eats popcorn while watching a movie.
entries.use: Watch a lively debate or unfolding drama without taking a side.
entries.avoid: Avoid treating real harm, harassment, or conflict as entertainment.

entries.label: Stephen Colbert eagerly makes popcorn
entries.alt: Stephen Colbert prepares popcorn with eager anticipation.
entries.use: Signal that an entertaining, low-stakes exchange is about to begin.
entries.avoid: Avoid serious disputes or interpersonal conflict.

entries.label: Kermit sipping tea
entries.alt: Kermit quietly sips from a cup.
entries.use: Signal playful detachment from harmless gossip or an obvious subtext.
entries.avoid: Avoid workplace politics, private information, or passive-aggressive conflict.
entries.search: Kermit sipping tea none of my business

entries.label: Why not both?
entries.alt: A girl lifts both hands to suggest choosing both options.
entries.use: Resolve a false choice when both options are genuinely compatible.
entries.avoid: Avoid when tradeoffs, budget, or scope make both impossible.

entries.label: Fry: shut up and take my money
entries.alt: Fry from Futurama thrusts cash forward and demands that it be taken.
entries.use: React to a product, idea, or feature you immediately want.
entries.avoid: Avoid financial pressure, procurement decisions, or sensitive spending.
entries.search: Futurama shut up take my money

entries.label: Elmo celebrating in flames
entries.alt: Elmo raises his arms triumphantly in front of animated flames.
entries.use: Celebrate harmless chaos or an intentionally wild result.
entries.avoid: Avoid fires, disasters, safety incidents, violence, or customer-impacting outages.

entries.label: Leonardo DiCaprio points at the screen
entries.alt: Leonardo DiCaprio sits up and points intently at a television.
entries.use: Spot a familiar reference, prediction, person, or pattern.
entries.avoid: Avoid pointing at a person's mistake or sensitive identity detail.

entries.label: Pedro Pascal laugh-cry
entries.alt: Pedro Pascal laughs and then looks overwhelmed as if laughing through tears.
entries.use: React to something simultaneously funny and painful in a low-stakes way.
entries.avoid: Avoid real grief, distress, or a person's vulnerable disclosure.

entries.label: Drake rejects one option and approves another
entries.alt: Drake turns away from one option and then smiles in approval at another.
entries.use: Contrast a bad option with a preferred alternative.
entries.avoid: Avoid oversimplifying nuanced tradeoffs or targeting a person's work.

entries.label: SpongeBob imagination rainbow
entries.alt: SpongeBob gestures overhead as a rainbow represents imagination.
entries.use: Celebrate creativity or lightly exaggerate an imaginative proposal.
entries.avoid: Avoid belittling a serious plan as fantasy.

entries.label: Ron Paul: it's happening
entries.alt: Ron Paul waves his arms excitedly beneath the words It's happening.
entries.use: Celebrate a long-predicted harmless event finally beginning.
entries.avoid: Avoid political ambiguity, workplace use, and serious breaking events.

entries.label: Animated spit-take laugh
entries.alt: An illustrated reaction spits out a drink while laughing.
entries.use: React to a genuinely funny or startling line.
entries.avoid: Avoid laughing at personal misfortune or a serious disclosure.

entries.label: Dr. Evil's theatrical laugh
entries.alt: Dr. Evil touches a pinky to his mouth and laughs theatrically.
entries.use: Frame a harmless clever plan as mock-villainous.
entries.avoid: Avoid security, privacy, manipulation, or actual wrongdoing.

entries.label: Making it rain
entries.alt: A cheerful person in sunglasses throws paper money into the air.
entries.use: Joke about a windfall, budget, or generous allocation among peers.
entries.avoid: Avoid financial hardship, compensation disputes, fundraising, or real spending pressure.

entries.label: Music-video WTF reaction
entries.alt: A music-video reaction expresses strong disbelief with profanity in its title and search context.
entries.use: Express strong disbelief with close peers who accept profanity.
entries.avoid: Avoid work, unknown audiences, minors, or any G-only request.

entries.label: Oprah: you get a car
entries.alt: Oprah excitedly gestures as if everyone is receiving a prize.
entries.use: Announce that everyone receives the same harmless benefit.
entries.avoid: Avoid promises, compensation, prizes, or benefits unless they are actually confirmed.
entries.search: Oprah you get a car everyone

entries.label: Jack Nicholson's gleeful nod
entries.alt: Jack Nicholson smiles and nods with delighted approval.
entries.use: Approve something with a mischievous edge.
entries.avoid: Avoid sexual, violent, or ethically questionable implications and unknown audiences.

entries.label: Proud slow clap
entries.alt: A man on a street gives a slow, proud clap.
entries.use: Give theatrical praise when the positive intent is clear.
entries.avoid: Avoid when slow clapping could read as mockery.
